p: Most day trips work reef country within about 15 nautical miles of the coast, so there's plenty of fishing time without a huge run. On calmer days and longer trips, boats head for the southern reefs of the Capricorn and Bunker Group, which lies roughly 45–75 km from the coastal departure ports.

Within about 15 nm of 1770: nannygai, sweetlip, cod, hussar and parrotfish, with red emperor, coral trout, cobia and mackerel
Bustard Head rocks
Rocks rising out of about 30 m of water north of 1770: mackerel, tuna, trevally, snapper in season and bottom fish
Trawler wrecks
Cobia, tuna, trevally and cod year-round
Lady Musgrave Island
The closest Bunker Group reef: coral trout and red throat emperor on the eastern side, red emperor in deeper water
Fitzroy and Lamont reefs
Pinnacles east of Fitzroy in 60–100 m hold schooling red emperor, mainly May–October
Boult and Hoskyn reefs
Deeper country to the east with red throat emperor, coral trout, cod and big pearl perch

Mangrove jack, barramundi, queenfish, grunter, flathead and whiting in the estuaries

p: You can fish 1770 all year, but local anglers rate the cooler months highest for the reef: bites improve as the water cools and the currents ease, and sharks are less of a problem around the outer reefs.

Best from about May to October, when schools gather on the pinnacles off Fitzroy Reef
Coral trout and red throat emperor
Year-round outside the coral reef fin fish closures
Cobia, tuna and trevally
Year-round around the wrecks

Off Bustard Head in the cooler months; closed 15 July–15 August

In the creeks; closed on the east coast 1 November–31 January

sections.h: Departure points and the Round Hill Creek bar
p: Charters leave from the Town of 1770 on Captain Cook Drive — from the marina, the public boat ramp and pontoon on Round Hill Creek, or by tender from the beach at the 1770 camping grounds. The creek mouth is very shallow and the bar moves constantly, so departure and return times are set around the tide. Operators check the tide height before confirming a trip, and VMR Round Hill can advise on current bar conditions.

Most of the offshore grounds are inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, and the Capricorn and Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones, especially on the western side. Charter skippers fish the open zones; if you're on your own boat, check the official GBRMPA zoning map rather than relying on the map at the ramp. Eurimbula Creek is a mud crab sanctuary.

Getting there: Agnes Water is about 5.5 hours' drive from Brisbane, around 1 hour 25 minutes from Bundaberg and 1 hour 30 minutes from Gladstone. The nearest airports are Bundaberg and Gladstone, and Greyhound coaches stop in Agnes Water daily. If you'd like more choice of boats, Bundaberg and Gladstone charters also fish the southern reefs.

faq: How far out is the reef from 1770?

Some of the reef fishing is close: charters work deep-water reefs within about 15 nautical miles of 1770. The Capricorn and Bunker Group, including Lady Musgrave Island and Fitzroy Reef, lies roughly 45–75 km from the coastal ports, so those trips are longer days.
Why do fishing charter times at 1770 depend on the tide?

Boats leave through Round Hill Creek, where the bar is shallow and keeps shifting. Operators time departures and returns for enough water over the bar and may reschedule if the tide is too low at the planned time.
Can you fish around Lady Musgrave Island?

In parts. Much of the Capricorn and Bunker Group is green zone, where fishing isn't allowed, but there are open zones around the reefs. Charter skippers know where you can fish; private boaties should check the GBRMPA zoning map first.
Is 1770 a good place to catch red emperor?
Yes — the area is known for it. Schools of red emperor gather on deep pinnacles east of Fitzroy Reef, mainly from about May to October, and they're also caught on the closer deep-water reefs.
Do I need to bring my own fishing gear?
No. Day charters from 1770 supply rods, reels, bait and tackle. Bring food and drinks if they're not included, sun protection and an esky for your catch.
agnes-water.season: 1770 fishes year-round, but locals rate the cooler months (about May to October) best for reef fish, with red emperor schooling on the Fitzroy Reef pinnacles. Cobia, tuna and trevally are on the wrecks all year. Note the closures: coral reef fin fish 8–12 October and 6–10 November (2026), snapper and pearl perch 15 July–15 August, and barramundi 1 November–31 January.

sections.h: Where the Mary River charters fish
p: The Mary River system lets one trip fish both fresh and salt water. Above the Shady Camp barrage are permanent, lily-lined billabongs; below it the tidal river splits into Sampan and Tommycut creeks and runs into Chambers Bay.

Where fresh water meets the tide — the best-known barra spot on the river, fished from boats and from the bank
Shady Camp billabong
Freshwater side: barramundi, saratoga and tarpon along the lilies, edges and rock bars
Sampan and Tommycut creek mouths
Big run-off barra trolled where floodwater pours out into Chambers Bay
Chambers Bay reefs and shoals
Reached from Shady Camp on neap tides: black jewfish, golden snapper, blue salmon and cod
Corroboree Billabong and Hardies Lagoon
A large billabong system closer to Darwin with about 45 km of fishable water: barra, saratoga and tarpon in the dry
Rockhole
Boat ramp in Mary River National Park giving access to the river channels

p: The Mary is fished most of the year, but the seasons change where and how you fish.

Peak time for big barra as the floodplains drain — below the barrage and at the creek mouths, best around March–April
Dry season (about May to September)
Consistent billabong fishing for barra, saratoga and tarpon; generally smaller fish
Build-up (September to mid-December)
Big barra move back to the river mouths and come back on the bite, especially on neap tides
Wet season
Big fish are possible between storms, but Shady Camp access is 4WD only

Arrive later in the run-off and through the build-up

p: The Mary River is east of Darwin via the Stuart and Arnhem Highways. Corroboree Billabong is about 108 km from Darwin, and Shady Camp is about 200 km — around 1 hour 40 minutes by car, or about two hours towing a boat. Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge, 20 minutes from Shady Camp, is reachable on sealed road almost all the way.

Most visitors fish with a Darwin-based guide on a day trip — pick-up from your Darwin accommodation is usually about 5am, fishing Corroboree or Shady Camp and returning mid to late afternoon. In the run-off, many guides run multi-day trips based at a lodge near Shady Camp.

The Mary River has its own fish management zone with a lower barramundi possession limit than the rest of the Territory and gear restrictions, including tighter rules close to the Shady Camp barrage. Check the current NT Fisheries rules before you go — your guide will also brief you. Recreational fishing below the barrage is open year-round.

You'll need an NT Parks Visitor Pass to enter Mary River National Park (NT residents are exempt), and campsites at Shady Camp must be booked online. The Mary has one of the highest densities of saltwater crocodiles in the world: don't swim, stay well back from the water's edge, and never wade in to free a snagged lure.

faq: How far is the Mary River from Darwin?

Corroboree Billabong is about 108 km east of Darwin, and Shady Camp is about 200 km — roughly 1 hour 40 minutes by car via the Stuart and Arnhem Highways. Most guided day trips pick up from Darwin accommodation at around 5am.
Can I do a Mary River fishing trip as a day trip from Darwin?

Yes. Several Darwin-based guides run day trips to Corroboree Billabong or Shady Camp with accommodation pick-up, returning mid to late afternoon. Run-off trips are often multi-day and based at a lodge near Shady Camp.
Can you fish from the bank at Shady Camp?
Yes — the barrage is a well-known land-based spot. Special gear rules apply close to the barrage wall, and crocodile numbers are very high, so keep well back from the edge.
Do I need a park pass for the Mary River?
Visitors need an NT Parks Visitor Pass for Mary River National Park; NT residents are exempt. Campsites, including at Shady Camp, must be booked online before you arrive.
Is there a closed season on the Mary River?
Not for recreational fishing below the Shady Camp barrage, which has been open year-round since 2014. The Mary River fish management zone does have its own possession limits and gear rules.
mary-river.season: The run-off from late February to May — peaking in March and April — is the time for big barramundi below the Shady Camp barrage and at the creek mouths. The build-up (September to mid-December) is the other big-fish window, while the dry season gives consistent billabong fishing for barra, saratoga and tarpon.

p: Central Coast charters work two different stretches of water. From The Haven at Terrigal, boats are on the offshore reefs within minutes, and game boats can run to the continental shelf, about 23 nautical miles out. From Hardys Bay on Broken Bay, charters fish the reefs and wrecks off the Bouddi Peninsula, or stay inside the bay around the headlands when the wind is up.
items: Terrigal offshore reefs
Year-round reef fishing for snapper, jewfish, kingfish, teraglin, morwong, flathead, trevally and John Dory
Browns Mountain
Seamount to the south that rises about 600 ft off the sea floor; a game-fishing ground
Norah Head Canyons
A series of deep trenches to the north, fished on game charters
Bouddi Peninsula reefs and wrecks
Reached from Hardys Bay; snapper, flathead, bream, jewfish, kingfish and tailor
Broken Bay headlands
Calm-water option for families and windy days

p: Reef fishing from Terrigal runs all year. Summer adds mahi mahi and the game season for marlin, yellowfin tuna and albacore; local game crews prefer to tag and release marlin. One Hardys Bay operator runs fishing charters only in the summer months, December to April, so check seasons before you plan a trip.
items: Snapper and reef fish
Year-round
Mahi mahi
Summer
Marlin
Seasonal game fishing; tag and release preferred
Yellowfin tuna and albacore
Game-charter targets in season
The Haven, Terrigal
Boat ramp at the south end of Terrigal Beach; plenty of parking, but keep clear of the trailer bays
Hardys Bay jetty
Corner of Killcare Road and Araluen Drive, opposite the shops; the gateway to Broken Bay and the Bouddi Peninsula

p: Licensed charter boats carry a block licence or fee-exemption certificate, so guests don't need their own NSW recreational fishing licence aboard. Shared trips need minimum numbers (five on one Central Coast boat), so wait until the trip is confirmed before booking accommodation.
Seasickness isn't grounds for a refund, and boats won't return early for one passenger, so take medication before you board. Terrigal is about an hour's drive north of Sydney.

faq: Can you still fish from the Central Coast when it's too rough offshore?
Often, yes. Hardys Bay charters can stay inside Broken Bay to fish the headlands and estuaries in calmer water, which is why one operator says its kids' trips are rarely cancelled for weather.
Where are the game-fishing grounds off the Central Coast?

Terrigal game boats fish Browns Mountain to the south and the Norah Head Canyons to the north. The continental shelf is about 23 nautical miles offshore, within range of boats qualified to 30 nautical miles.
Do Central Coast fishing charters run all year?
Reef charters from Terrigal run year-round, but at least one Hardys Bay operator runs fishing charters only from December to April, so check the season when booking.
How do I get to Terrigal for a fishing charter?

Terrigal is about an hour's drive north of Sydney. Take the Gosford exit off the M1 Pacific Motorway, follow the signs to Terrigal, and turn into The Haven at the south end of the beach, past the football field to the boat ramp.

p: Newcastle's charters are mostly small-boat estuary guides. They fish the Hunter River from Newcastle Harbour upstream towards Raymond Terrace, and Lake Macquarie, a coastal lake of more than 100 sq km joined to the sea by the narrow Swansea Channel. Offshore reef boats work out of Swansea.

Wrecks, oyster beds and rock walls; lure fishing for dusky flathead and mulloway
Lake Macquarie
About 24 km long and up to around 11 m deep; flathead, bream and whiting are the 'big three', with mulloway and kingfish the prized sportfish
Swansea Channel, Swansea Bridge and the 'Drop Over'
Kingfish on surface lures or live bait; Australian salmon school in the channel in the cooler months
Offshore reefs off Swansea
Reef trips of four to seven hours and a 10-hour deep-reef run from about 85 m to 140 m
Newcastle Offshore Artificial Reef
DPI reef in about 28.5 m, expected to hold kingfish, snapper, silver trevally and mulloway

p: The estuary fishery runs all year. Guides run twilight sessions aimed at mulloway, and schools of Australian salmon settle in Swansea Channel in the cooler months.

Year-round; trophy fish of 70–80 cm are taken on lures
Mulloway (jewfish)

Australian salmon
Cooler months in Swansea Channel
Kingfish
Around Swansea Bridge and the Drop Over

p: Lake Macquarie hasn't been commercially fished or netted since 2002, and NSW bag and size limits apply. Some Newcastle guides fish lures only and promote catch and release, so ask before booking if you want to keep a feed.
Newcastle is at least two hours' drive north of central Sydney on the M1, and Newcastle Airport at Williamtown has flights from major Australian cities.

faq: Is there a calm-water fishing charter in Newcastle for kids?

Yes. Capn's Charters runs a three-hour kids' charter in calm water on the Hunter River for three children aged 6–16, or two kids and an adult, and Day Trippin fishes sheltered Lake Macquarie with up to four guests.
Where are kingfish caught near Swansea?
Around Swansea Bridge and the 'Drop Over', where the channel meets Lake Macquarie, on surface lures or live bait.
Can you go offshore fishing from Newcastle?
Yes. Swansea-based boats run outside-reef trips of four to seven hours and a 10-hour deep-reef trip that starts in about 85 m and finishes around 140 m.
How big is Lake Macquarie?
NSW DPI describes it as Australia's largest coastal saltwater lake. It covers more than 100 sq km, is about 24 km long, and has 29 public boat ramps around a 174 km foreshore.

p: Port Stephens pairs a large, sheltered estuary with quick access to offshore islands and the continental shelf. Reef boats leave through Tomaree and Yacaaba heads for Cabbage Tree, Boondelbah, Little and Broughton islands, while game boats fish the FADs about 20 km out, the Big Gibber to the north and the shelf beyond.

Reef fishing for snapper and pearl perch; also a barbecue stop on family game days
Cabbage Tree Island
Reef fish just outside the heads; sheltered water nearby for kids' sessions
Little Island and Fingal Head
Soft-plastic snapper grounds
FADs (about 20 km out) and the 120 m line
Black and striped marlin and mahi mahi, December to March

Black and striped marlin when the fish move in
Port Stephens estuary
Main basin plus the Myall, Karuah and Tilligerry systems; flathead, bream, whiting, mulloway, kingfish and longtail tuna

p: Port Stephens hosts the NSW Interclub, Australia's biggest game fishing tournament, and is one of the few places where blue, black and striped marlin can all be caught in one day. Summer and early autumn are marlin time; tuna take over wide of the port from autumn into winter.

Late spring through summer; mostly 30–100 kg fish riding the East Australian Current
Striped marlin
December to March, often in packs on bait balls

January to March over the shelf
Mahi mahi

p: Port Stephens is about 2.5 hours' drive north of Sydney. Some reef charters set a minimum age of 12, while others run sheltered kids' sessions, so match the trip to your group.
The waterway is a marine park, and estuary guides explain the park and its wildlife on the trip. Several Port Stephens charters include NSW fishing licences for their guests.

faq: Can you catch all three marlin species in one day at Port Stephens?
It's possible. Port Stephens is one of the few places where blue, black and striped marlin can all be encountered, and game crews chase a single-day grand slam in summer.
What can you catch inside Port Stephens without going offshore?

Depending on the month, the estuary holds bream, flathead, whiting, luderick, mulloway, tailor, salmon, kingfish, squid and even longtail tuna. The Myall, Karuah and Tilligerry tributaries give shelter when the bay is choppy.
How far out are the marlin grounds from Port Stephens?
Light-tackle boats run about 20 km to the FAD region or north to the Big Gibber. Blue marlin trips go out over the continental shelf.
Are there kids' fishing charters in Port Stephens?
Yes. Options include a two-hour estuary trip for under-10s and a 3.5-hour family morning in sheltered water near Cabbage Tree Island or Fingal.

p: Port Macquarie charters split between offshore reef trips from the town centre and guided lure fishing on the region's rivers. The Hastings River, a NSW Recreational Fishing Haven, is tidal for about 32 km to just upstream of Wauchope, and guides also travel to the Maria, Macleay and Manning rivers.

Six-hour deep-sea trips for snapper, pearl perch, kingfish, flathead and mahi mahi
Hastings River
Dusky flathead, mulloway, bream, whiting and tailor on lures
Maria River and Limeburners Creek
Hastings tributaries popular with boat anglers; the Maria (about 20 minutes away) is a bass river
Macleay River
About 40 minutes from Port Macquarie; bass, flathead and mulloway
Manning River at Harrington
Flathead, bream, whiting and mulloway

p: There is something to catch all year. Spring and summer are the main offshore seasons, while beach and rock fishing for tailor, bream and mulloway is popular in autumn and winter.

Year-round; fish of 70–90 cm-plus are caught regularly
Mulloway
Year-round in the Hastings and nearby rivers
Whiting
About October to March or April on the sand flats
Australian bass
September to May; catch and release on guided trips

Offshore reefs; spring and summer are the main seasons

Warmer months offshore
Town Green boardwalk, Short Street car park end
74 Clarence Street; free parking; offshore boats leave 5–6 am most days
McInherney Park boat ramp
Off River Park Road; estuary guide meeting point, 6 am in spring and summer, 7 am in autumn and winter

p: Humpback whales are often seen from offshore charters during the migration. On guided estuary trips Australian bass are released, and at least one guide can't clean fish on board, so bring a bucket or cooler.
Families who just want to throw a line in can fish the town wharf, the Settlement Point picnic area or the southern breakwall.

faq: How far up the Hastings River can you fish?
The Hastings is tidal for about 32 km inland, to just upstream of Wauchope. Most anglers fish the estuary and lower reaches, with freshwater bass in the upper river.
Can you fish for Australian bass near Port Macquarie?
Yes. Guided bass trips run from September to May on the Maria River, about 20 minutes from Port Macquarie, or the Macleay, about 40 minutes away. Bass are catch and release.
Where can families fish without a boat in Port Macquarie?

The town wharf and the wharves beside the Short Street charter berth suit families. Settlement Point picnic area produces whiting, bream and flathead, and the southern breakwall holds tailor, bream, mulloway and luderick.

p: South West Rocks has unusually quick access to deep water. The first ocean reef is about ten minutes from the bar, most fishing is 1–5 km out, and the continental shelf is only about 12 nautical miles off Laggers Point, so the East Australian Current can push warm water right up to the rocks.
items: Fish Rock
Rises from about 30 m of water off Smoky Cape; resident kingfish all year. Marine-park zone: no bait fishing within 200 m
Green Island and Black Rock
The other Smoky Cape islands; Green Island has the same 200 m no-bait rule
Gaol Grounds
Near-shore sport grounds known for black marlin, wahoo, mahi mahi and cobia, usually after Christmas
Reefs from Nambucca Heads to Hungry Head
From 5 m to over 200 m deep; snapper, pearl perch, teraglin, tuskfish and mulloway
Shelf canyons
Three deep canyons near the shelf that hold blue marlin
Macleay River
Estuary fall-back for flathead, mulloway, bream, whiting and mangrove jack

p: As a rough guide, warm-water species such as mackerel are caught from about January to May, and cooler-water species such as snapper and kingfish from May to December, with plenty of overlap.

Late winter, peaking in spring
Yellowfin tuna
Large fish on the shelf in winter and spring

Best in November and December

Base of the small-group sportfishing charter

p: Fish Rock and Green Island are marine-park zones protecting grey nurse sharks: no bait fishing within 200 m, though lures are allowed. Trips cross the Macleay River bar; operators reschedule for strong wind or big seas, but usually not for rain.
South West Rocks sits roughly halfway between Sydney and Brisbane on the Mid North Coast, and fishing-and-accommodation packages are available for groups.

faq: Can you fish with bait at Fish Rock?
No. Fish Rock and Green Island are marine-park zones protecting grey nurse sharks, so bait fishing isn't allowed within 200 m. Lures are fine.
How far offshore is the continental shelf at South West Rocks?
Only about 12 nautical miles off Laggers Point, one of its closest points to the east coast. That is why marlin, wahoo and mahi mahi can turn up very close to shore.
What happens if it's too rough to fish offshore at South West Rocks?
Guides can switch to the Macleay River estuary, which holds flathead, mulloway, bream, whiting, trevally and mangrove jack and stays fishable when the sea isn't.

p: Yamba and Iluka sit either side of the Clarence River mouth. Offshore charters range from Evans Head in the north to Sandon in the south and out towards the continental shelf, but most reef trips fish 5–10 km off the Clarence River bar, with the skipper picking from more than 20 spots once over the bar.

Most trips fish 5–10 km out for snapper, pearl perch, flathead, mulloway, morwong and trevally
Evans Head to Sandon
The wider range covered by the larger charter boat, out towards the shelf
Wooli grounds
Southern grounds fished by local skippers
Woody Head to Angourie
Coastline used for seasonal humpback whale cruises

p: Morning reef trips run seven days a week in every season, weather permitting, and twilight trips run from 1 pm to sunset. Lures are run for surface fish when they show up.

The main offshore reef targets
Mulloway and flathead

Offshore target

Seasonal cruises during the migration

Shared trips collect from several points, usually leaving around 6 am

p: Every offshore trip crosses the Clarence River bar, and life vests must be worn during bar crossings. Skippers usually make the weather call by about 8 pm the night before; weather cancellations get a refund or a rebooking.
Bring an esky with ice to leave in the car, as fish are kept on ice aboard. Children under five can't be taken on at least one boat.

faq: How far offshore do Yamba fishing charters go?
Most reef trips fish 5–10 km off the Clarence River bar, choosing from more than 20 spots on the day. The larger boat ranges from Evans Head to Sandon and out towards the continental shelf.
Can you get picked up from Iluka for a Yamba fishing charter?
Yes. Both Yamba operators offer Iluka pick-ups: one from the Iluka Boatshed on request, the other from pick-up points around Yamba and Iluka.
Do Yamba fishing charters cross the Clarence River bar?
Yes. Offshore trips cross the bar, and life vests must be worn during the crossing. Skippers decide where to fish once they're over the bar and can judge the wind, current and tide.
yamba.season: Morning reef trips run seven days a week in every season, weather permitting, for snapper, pearl perch, flathead and mulloway. Lures are run for kingfish, mackerel, tailor and salmon when surface fish appear, and humpback whale cruises operate during the migration.

p: Charters on this stretch of coast leave from Brunswick Heads, about 15 minutes north of Byron Bay, and Evans Head, between Ballina and Yamba. Brunswick Heads boats fish the reefs off Byron for snapper, pearl perch, jewfish and kingfish and chase pelagics wider out, while Evans Head specialises in deep-water pearl perch about 30 km offshore.

Pearl perch and snapper in about 80 m, roughly 30 km offshore; also jewfish, samsonfish, kingfish and teraglin
Reefs off Brunswick Heads and Byron Bay

Ballina Offshore Artificial Reef
Two steel towers in 32 m, about 5 km south of the Richmond River mouth, deployed in March 2026

p: Pearl perch and reef fish are caught through the year, and the warmer months add mackerel, wahoo, tuna and marlin. Humpback whales pass the NSW coast heading north from about May to July and back south from September to November, and are often seen from fishing boats.

p: Trips are confirmed the evening or afternoon before, once sea conditions (and, at Brunswick Heads, the bar) have been checked; weather cancellations are refunded or moved. Evans Head also offers week-long midweek packages with accommodation for groups.
Evans Head trips supply bait and tackle, but you bring food, drinks and an esky; Byron Bay Charters supplies gear, bait and soft drinks.

faq: Is there a new artificial reef off Ballina?
Yes. NSW DPI deployed an offshore artificial reef in March 2026: two steel towers in 32 m of water about 5 km south of the Richmond River mouth, expected to attract mackerel, snapper and mulloway.
How far offshore is the pearl perch fishing at Evans Head?
Evans Head charters target pearl perch and snapper in about 80 m of water, roughly 30 km offshore, with eight-hour trips going wider when the weather allows.
Where do Byron Bay fishing charters leave from?
Byron Bay Charters runs from the Brunswick Heads jetty in the Boat Harbour, about 15 minutes north of Byron Bay, leaving at 6 am for full-day trips.

p: Lord Howe Island sits on the world's southernmost coral reef, where the East Australian Current pushes deep water up the island's slopes and tropical and temperate fish share the same water. The island is surrounded by marine park with no commercial fishery. Charters fish the island shelf and reef edges close in, and the drop-offs, seamounts and Balls Pyramid further out.

Kingfish on jigs and stickbaits, trevally and reef species on four- to six-hour trips
Balls Pyramid
The world's tallest sea stack, 552 m high and about 23 km from the island; big kingfish, yellowfin and wahoo
Seamounts and drop-offs

The Lagoon

Jetty, beaches and rock platforms
Land-based options; garfish off the jetty are a local favourite

p: Kingfish are caught year-round, but winter is the best of it, which runs against the summer visitor season. Summer brings calmer water and long evenings.

p: The waters are a marine park: spearfishing is banned, bag limits apply to bluefish and double headers, and catch and release is encouraged. Sharks take hooked fish fairly often, so expect to lose a few.
Flights to the island are weather-affected more often than most, so book fishing early in your stay to leave room to reschedule, and consider travel insurance. Phone reception offshore is unreliable.

faq: How far is Balls Pyramid from Lord Howe Island?
About 23 km. The 552 m sea stack is the world's tallest, and charters run five-hour shared or sole-use trips to fish around it, as well as full-day offshore trips.
Why do Lord Howe fishing charter times change each day?
Boats leave from the jetty inside the lagoon and can't get out on a very low tide (one operator's limit is about 0.3 m), so departure times shift with the tides through the week.
Can you spearfish at Lord Howe Island?
No. Spearfishing is banned in the Lord Howe Island Marine Park, and bag limits apply to some lagoon species such as bluefish and double header.
What is the Lord Howe lagoon grand slam?

Catching a trevally, silver drummer, bluefish and the endemic double header wrasse in one session of sight-casting in the shallow lagoon. Bag limits apply to bluefish and double headers, and catch and release is encouraged.

p: Sydney charters split into harbour trips and offshore trips. Harbour guides fish Sydney Harbour itself for kingfish and jewfish, often within sight of the Opera House, while offshore boats run out through the Heads, or from Cronulla and Port Botany in the south, to reefs roughly 1 to 12 nautical miles out in 30 to 120 m of water. Sport and game boats troll the named reefs and the NSW DPI fish aggregating devices (FADs) for kingfish, mahi mahi, tuna and marlin.

p: There is something to chase off Sydney all year, but the target changes with the East Australian Current. Warm summer water brings pelagics close in; winter brings tuna, deep-water species and snapper on the inshore reefs.

p: Most Sydney charters supply rods, bait and licence cover, but check what your trip includes. Several offshore operators say they will not return early for seasickness, so take a preventative if you are prone to it. Age limits vary: Sydney Charter Fishing does not take children under eight, and Sydney Premium Charters' shared and mahi mahi trips are for ages 12 and up, while its private trips have no age limit.

faq: Can you catch kingfish in Sydney Harbour?
Yes. Kingfish are a year-round option in Sydney Harbour, and fish over a metre are not uncommon. Harbour guides use live squid and stickbait lures, and the best run is from spring into early summer.
Can I join a Sydney fishing charter on my own?

Yes. Shared seats are sold by Deep Blue Charters at Rose Bay ($200 half-day reef), Sydney Charter Fishing at Manly ($240-$280), Sydney Premium Charters at Cronulla on weekends ($260), and Cronulla Reef Fishing Charters runs a full-day reef trip for individuals. Some shared trips need a minimum number of anglers to run.
When is marlin season off Sydney?

Mainly summer and autumn. Small black marlin turn up on the inshore reefs from around Christmas, striped marlin peak in summer, and blue marlin are most likely late in summer and into autumn, when the biggest fish are caught. Striped marlin are occasionally caught in winter too.
How far offshore do Sydney reef fishing trips go?

Most reef trips fish between about 1 and 12 nautical miles off the coast in 30 to 120 m of water. Mahi mahi trips run about 20 km offshore to the FADs, and deep-drop trips go further out to Browns Mountain.
sydney.season: There is fishing off Sydney all year. Kingfish are caught year-round but peak from spring into early summer, and jewfish fire in the harbour from October to July. Summer brings mahi mahi to the FADs and black marlin from around Christmas, with blue marlin best late in summer and into autumn. Winter is the time for yellowfin and albacore tuna, gemfish, blue-eye trevalla and snapper on the inshore reefs.

p: Illawarra charters drift the reefs along the coast between Stanwell Park and Shellharbour, from just off the beach to about 10 nautical miles out. From Kiama the boat is in open ocean almost as soon as it leaves the harbour, with reef grounds within about 15 km and the continental shelf about 30 km offshore for deep-water and game fishing.

Age guidance varies: Aquilla runs short Junior Angler sessions for kids aged 8 to 16 in school holidays, while Kiama Charter Service doesn't recommend its eight-hour days for children under 10. Kiama takes bookings by phone only, and weekends between September and Christmas often book out well ahead.

faq: Can you go overnight fishing from Wollongong?
Yes. Five Island Charters runs overnight game charters on Seafox, a 40 ft flybridge cruiser that sleeps six plus crew, for $4,850 for the boat.
Where do I park for a fishing charter at Wollongong Harbour?

Aquilla Fishing Charters says there is free all-day street parking beside the marina just below Endeavour Drive, and more free all-day parking near Flagstaff Point (Wollongong Head) lighthouse, about a five-minute walk from Belmore Basin.
How far out is the continental shelf from Kiama?
About 30 km. Kiama Charter Service's deep sea trips fish the shelf in water up to 400 m deep for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku, mainly from May to September, and you can still see land.
Are there fishing trips for kids in Wollongong?
Yes. Aquilla Fishing Charters runs two-hour Junior Angler school-holiday sessions for kids aged 8 to 16, with a supervising adult included in the booking. Dates are posted on its social media.
wollongong.season: Reef fishing for snapper, morwong, flathead and pigfish runs all year. Game boats chase marlin, mahi mahi, mako sharks, yellowfin and wahoo from December to April, then yellowfin, bluefin and albacore tuna from June to October. Deep-sea trips to the shelf for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku run in the cooler months, roughly May to September.

p: Jervis Bay is a marine park with sheltered water inside the bay and deep water right outside it, and the continental shelf is close by. Charters fish the reefs off the bay and the Shoalhaven coast for table fish, and head wider for pelagics and deep-water species.

Jervis Bay is about two hours' drive from both Sydney and Canberra. On JB Fishing Charters' trips you bring your own hat, sunglasses, food and drinks.

faq: Is Jervis Bay a marine park?

Yes. Jervis Bay Marine Park has zoning rules that control where and how you can fish. NSW DPI suggests checking the zoning map or the FishSmart app before fishing, and spearfishing is banned in the creeks and sanctuary zones. Charter skippers know the boundaries.
How far is Jervis Bay from Sydney and Canberra?
About two hours' drive from either city, according to JB Fishing Charters. Greenwell Point, home of Escape Fishing Charters, is about two hours south of Sydney and 20 minutes north of Jervis Bay.
Can you catch squid in Jervis Bay?
Yes. NSW DPI describes Jervis Bay as renowned for squid over the seagrass edges, along with good bottom fishing for snapper.
Is there a cheaper rate for kids on Jervis Bay fishing charters?
JB Fishing Charters charges $120 for children under 12 on its full-day deep sea trip, half the $240 adult price.

p: Three ports cover this stretch of the South Coast. Batemans Bay boats fish the reefs in and around the bay and run about 22 km out to the continental shelf for game fish and deep-drop fishing. Narooma boats work the reefs between the town and Barunguba (Montague Island), about 9 km offshore, and the shelf roughly 20 km out. Further south, Bermagui boats fish for reef fish, kingfish, yellowfin tuna, sharks and deep-water table fish.

All three charter operators here include fishing licence cover for their passengers. Narooma Charters asks you to bring your own food and drink, while Game On and FishBermi supply tea, coffee and light snacks or morning tea, with meals by arrangement. Bring an esky or cooler bag to take your catch home.

faq: How far is Montague Island from Narooma?
Barunguba (Montague Island) is about 9 km offshore from Narooma, around a 20-minute run by charter boat. Narooma's town wharf is the closest port to the island.
How far is the continental shelf from Batemans Bay and Narooma?
Game On Charters says the shelf is about 22 km from the Batemans Bay marina. Off Narooma it is around 20 km out, with Montague Island roughly halfway.
When is marlin season on the South Coast near Narooma?

Narooma Charters puts the game season at December to June. Striped and black marlin are around from about Christmas until the water cools in June, and yellowfin and albacore tuna are best in late autumn.
Can you go deep-drop fishing from Batemans Bay or Bermagui?

Yes. Game On Charters runs full-day shared or private deep-drop trips from Batemans Bay with Shimano electric reels, and FishBermi in Bermagui offers trips for deep-water table fish such as gemfish and blue-eye trevalla.
intro: Three charter ports cover this part of the NSW South Coast. Batemans Bay boats leave d'Albora Marina to fish the reefs in and around the bay for snapper, kingfish, morwong and flathead, and run about 22 km out to the continental shelf for game fish and deep dropping. Narooma's town wharf is the closest port to Barunguba (Montague Island), about 9 km offshore and a well-known reef and game fishing area.
Further south, Bermagui boats leave O'Shea Wharf for reef fish, kingfish, yellowfin tuna, sharks and deep-water gemfish and blue-eye trevalla.
batemans-bay.season: Reef fish such as snapper, morwong, flathead and kingfish are caught all year around Montague Island and the Batemans Bay reefs. The offshore game season runs from about December to June: marlin from around Christmas until the water cools in June, and yellowfin and albacore tuna best in late autumn.

p: Eden boats work Twofold Bay and the inshore reefs for snapper, morwong, leatherjackets and flathead, run a few minutes south to the kingfish grounds around Mowarry Point and Green Cape, and head out to the continental shelf for game fish. Merimbula operators fish the local reefs off Merimbula Bay on shorter trips, while the sheltered lakes offer calm-water flathead fishing.

Humpback whales pass close to shore during the May to November migration, and boats must keep at least 100 m from adult whales. Twofold Bay has an active Navy wharf, and exclusion zones apply when Navy ships are alongside. Charters that include licence cover mean you do not need your own NSW recreational fishing licence on board.

faq: Does Eden have a bar crossing?
No. Visit Eden describes Twofold Bay as the Southern Hemisphere's third-deepest harbour, with no bar to cross, so Eden charters can head out in conditions that keep bar ports closed.
When is the game fishing season at Eden?

Visit Eden puts the main game season at November to the end of July, with marlin, yellowfin, albacore and striped tuna, sharks and broadbill. Trade-A-Boat notes January to late March often fishes best for marlin.
When are the kingfish around Eden?
Freedom Charters runs its kingfish-focused sports trips from about November to June in 'kingie country' south of Eden, where most fish are 5 to 8 kg.
Is there a short fishing trip for families at Merimbula?
Yes. Sapphire Coastal Adventures runs a three-hour reef charter from the Merimbula Public Jetty, and Fishpen Charters runs three-hour trips from Mitchies Jetty that are popular with families.
How far is Merimbula from Sydney and Canberra?

Merimbula is about 454 km south of Sydney on the Princes Highway and 243 km from Canberra. Merimbula Regional Airport has daily Rex and Qantas flights to Sydney and Melbourne, and Eden is a further 30 minutes south.

sections.h: Fishing regions along the NSW coast
p: NSW charters fall into a few broad regions. On the North Coast, where tropical and temperate currents meet, reef trips for snapper and pearl perch mix with mackerel, mahi mahi and marlin. Port Stephens, Newcastle and the Central Coast pair big estuaries and lakes with offshore reefs and a strong marlin season. Sydney and the Illawarra offer harbour, reef and shelf fishing close to the city, and the South Coast has deep water close to shore, island reefs and a long game season.

Summer and early autumn are the main game-fishing months, when warm currents bring marlin and mahi mahi within reach, and the season runs later the further south you go. In the cooler months, southern boats run deep-drop trips for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku, and yellowfin and albacore tuna turn up off Sydney and the South Coast.

p: Many NSW charters include licence cover for their passengers, but not all do: Reel Adventure Fishing in Sydney, for example, asks every angler to buy their own NSW recreational fishing licence, so check before you go. Several stretches of coast are marine parks with zoning rules, including Cape Byron, the Solitary Islands, Jervis Bay, Batemans and Lord Howe Island. NSW DPI recommends checking the zoning map or the FishSmart app; charter skippers know the boundaries.

faq: Where can you catch marlin in NSW?

Marlin are targeted from Tweed Heads to Eden. Port Stephens is one of the few places where black, striped and blue marlin can be caught on the same day, Sydney boats chase them through summer and autumn, and Eden's game season runs from November to the end of July.
Are there marine parks on the NSW coast?

Yes. They include Cape Byron, the Solitary Islands (the oldest marine park in NSW), Jervis Bay, Batemans and Lord Howe Island. Each has zoning rules about where and how you can fish, which charter skippers follow. NSW DPI's FishSmart app shows the zones.
Where can you go deep-drop fishing in NSW?

Kiama Charter Service runs deep sea trips to the shelf about 30 km out, in water up to 400 m, from May to September. Batemans Bay and Bermagui boats also fish deep water for blue-eye trevalla and gemfish, and Sydney boats drop on Browns Mountain in winter.

p: Darwin sits on a peninsula with Darwin Harbour to the west, the Timor Sea to the north and Shoal Bay to the east, so guides can usually find a sheltered launch whatever the wind. The harbour itself is many times the size of Sydney Harbour, with three main arms full of mangrove creeks, and its Second World War and Cyclone Tracy wrecks hold black jewfish.

Half-day trips mostly stay inside the harbour. Full-day and extended bluewater trips run out to reefs 20–50 km offshore, while barra guides drive clients to Shoal Bay, Bynoe Harbour, the Adelaide River or the Mary River billabongs.

p: Tides of 6–7 metres are common, so departure times and fishing spots move with the tide; confirm your start time when you book. Saltwater crocodiles live in the harbour and creeks, so stay back from the water's edge at ramps and never swim. Sandflies are common at ramps and in the harbour mangroves: long light pants, socks and repellent help.

Bag and size limits apply to most species, so check the current NT Fisheries rules or the free NT Fishing Mate app before keeping fish. The annual Million Dollar Fish competition releases tagged barramundi across the Top End each season, and several Darwin operators promote it.

faq: Do Darwin fishing charters pick you up from your hotel?

Barra day tours usually do: operators such as Barra Private Tours, DNA Barra Fishing, Obsession and River & Reef collect guests around 4:30–5am. Harbour and bluewater trips generally meet at the wharf or ramp (Stokes Hill Wharf, Cullen Bay or Dinah Beach). Barra or Blue charges $50 per person for return transfers.
Can you do a Mary River barra trip as a day trip from Darwin?

Yes. Corroboree Billabong, part of the Mary River system, is about 1.5 hours' drive from Darwin, and several Darwin operators run full-day billabong trips with pre-dawn hotel pick-up, returning mid to late afternoon. Shady Camp is further, about two hours or more.
How big are the tides in Darwin?
Tides of 6–7 metres are common, which strongly affects where and when charters fish. Local boats are built to handle them, and departure times are set around the tide rather than a fixed schedule.
Can I take my fish home on the plane from Darwin?

Often, yes. Several operators fillet and bag the catch, and some, such as Offshore Boats, will freeze and pack it in airline-approved seafood boxes on request. Otherwise bring an esky or insulated cooler bag, and keep within NT possession limits.
Are there crocodiles in Darwin Harbour?

Yes. NT tourism describes the harbour as dotted with shipwrecks, mangroves and saltwater crocodiles. Charter boats are a safe platform, but don't swim, and keep well back from the water's edge at ramps and creek banks.

Pick-up for DNA Barra Fishing's 2–14 day run-off trips

Check river conditions and the daily access report if launching your own boat; passes can be bought here too

p: A Kakadu park pass, sold by Parks Australia, is valid for 7 days. Dry-season rates (15 May–31 October) are $40 per adult and tropical-summer rates $25; passes bought for 1 July to 31 October 2026 are charged at wet-season rates, and NT residents are free. The pass covers Kakadu only. Guided tours may include entry permits, so ask your operator.
Saltwater crocodiles are present throughout the rivers. Weather can change quickly, so check the access report and the Bureau of Meteorology radar, and keep your trip flexible.

faq: Which fishing guides can operate inside Kakadu National Park?

Only licensed operators who meet the park's criteria. DNA Barra Fishing says it is one of the few guides approved to fish the park, and Kakadu Fishing Tours describes itself as one of a select few operators and the only one based full time in Kakadu.
How far is Kakadu from Darwin for a fishing trip?
Jabiru, the base for Kakadu fishing tours, is about a 2.5-hour drive from Darwin. Because of the travel time, DNA Barra Fishing's Kakadu trips run for two days or more.
Can you fish Kakadu in the wet season?

Most fishing operators close during the tropical summer, but NT tourism notes you can still fish Yellow Water on the South Alligator floodplain, which has a boat ramp. The park is open all year, though flooding closes some areas, so check the Kakadu Access Report.
Can you catch saltwater barra at Cahill's Crossing?

Above the crossing, yes: Kakadu Fishing Tours fishes the East Alligator just upstream, where both freshwater and saltwater barramundi are caught. Saltwater crocodiles share the river, so fish from the boat with your guide.

p: The Daly is one of the Territory's top barramundi rivers and is reserved for recreational fishing, with no commercial barra fishing. Lined with rainforest and paperbarks, its fallen trees make classic barra snags. The river runs more than 40 km from the Daly River crossing to Anson Bay, through the Daly–Reynolds floodplain system, which has the largest catchment of any major freshwater floodplain in the NT.

p: The run-off, roughly March to May, is the classic window, but only about two tide cycles a month suit it, so the best dates book out early.

p: The Daly is about 210–223 km south-west of Darwin, roughly 2.5 hours via the Stuart Highway and Daly River Road. The river can rise and fall by up to 16 m with the seasons and tides of up to 7 m are common, so local knowledge matters. Both freshwater and saltwater crocodiles live in the river.

NT tourism notes the lower tidal section is closed to fishing from 1 October to 31 January; check the current NT Fisheries rules for the exact boundaries and limits before you go. Wet-season trips can be redirected if cyclones or flooding cut access.

faq: How far is the Daly River from Darwin?
About 210–223 km south-west, roughly a 2.5-hour drive via the Stuart Highway and Daly River Road. It is about 110 km south-west of Adelaide River.
Is the Daly River closed to fishing at any time of year?

NT tourism says the lower tidal section of the Daly is closed to fishing from 1 October to 31 January. Check the current NT Fisheries rules for the exact closure area before planning a trip in those months.
Can you fish the Daly River from a mothership?

Yes. Humbug Fishing runs 5–7 day liveaboard trips from Darwin on its 24 m catamaran Starfire, fishing the Daly River mouth, Anson Bay and the Reynolds floodplains from surveyed tenders, with hotel transfers included.
Are there crocodiles in the Daly River?
Yes, a healthy population of both freshwater and saltwater crocodiles. Fish from a boat or well back from the bank, and never swim.

p: The Dundee Coast runs from Native Point to the Peron Islands and is known as the best bluewater fishing within easy reach of Darwin. Some very big black jewfish are caught less than 2 km out, barra are taken along the coast and in the rivers, and wider reefs produce coral trout, red emperor, Spanish mackerel and cobia.

p: Barra can be caught any time; NT tourism calls October the 'sweet spot' when tides suit. Anglers Choice says dry-season barra average 65–80 cm, with metre-plus fish more likely in the run-off and build-up.

p: Dundee Beach is about 90 minutes from Darwin by sealed road, with a beachfront tavern, holiday park and boat ramp. Several operators have their own accommodation for multi-day packages. Boats in 2C survey can fish up to 15 nautical miles offshore, which opens up the wider reefs.

Bynoe Harbour sits in a 'storm alley', so watch the Bureau of Meteorology radar. Saltwater crocodiles are present in the rivers and creeks. Check tides before booking flights, and check the current NT Fisheries rules for bag and size limits.

faq: How far is Dundee Beach from Darwin?
About 90 minutes by sealed road, according to NT tourism; local operators quote 140–165 km. By sea it can be quicker, depending on the weather.
Can I stay at Dundee Beach on a fishing package?

Yes. Dundee Beach Fishing Charters' retreat sleeps up to 16 with a pool and chef, Anglers Choice has its own beach house, and Barra or Blue has a five-bedroom house with a pool. All include Darwin transfers on multi-day packages.
Why do some Dundee charters fish further offshore than others?
It depends on survey class. Anglers Choice and Dundee Beach Fishing Charters run boats in 2C survey, which lets them fish up to 15 nautical miles offshore and reach the wider reefs.
Is Bynoe Harbour safe for small boats?
Much of Bynoe Harbour is considered sheltered water and can be fished from a small tinny, but it sits in a storm alley, so locals keep an eye on the Bureau of Meteorology radar throughout the day.

p: Bathurst and Melville islands, about 80 km north of Darwin, offer estuary fishing for barramundi, salmon and mangrove jack and bluewater fishing around rocky headlands for queenfish, giant trevally, golden snapper and black jewfish. Day boats run up from Leaders Creek, while fly-in guests fish from Port Hurd on western Bathurst Island.

p: The Tiwi Islands are Aboriginal land and access needs a permit; the Tiwi Land Council manages permits, and guided operators and the Retreat include or arrange what visitors need. The annual football grand final and art sale in March is the only day permits are not required to travel to the islands.
Saltwater crocodiles are common and box jellyfish are present from October to May, so swimming in the sea is off the menu.

faq: How do you get to the Tiwi Islands to go fishing?

Most day trips launch at Leaders Creek, about an hour's drive from Darwin, and run past the Vernon Islands to the Tiwis. Alternatively, fly from Darwin to Port Hurd on a charter flight and stay at Tiwi Island Retreat. NT tourism says travel is by light aircraft or ferry.
When do Tiwi Islands fishing operators close?
Most close during the tropical summer (wet season). Tiwi Island Retreat closes every year from December to March, though it takes bookings year-round.
Can you catch marlin and sailfish off the Tiwi Islands?
Yes. NT tourism names the Bathurst trench north-west of Bathurst Island, Afghan Shoals south of Cape Fourcroy and Shepparton Shoals to the west as marlin and sailfish grounds.
Can you swim at the Tiwi Islands?
Not in the sea. Tiwi Island Retreat warns that saltwater crocodiles are common and box jellyfish are present from October to May; guests use its beachfront pool instead.

p: Arnhem Land's coast is cut by dozens of remote tidal rivers that visitors can only reach with permits, which is why most anglers fish with an accredited operator: a day charter out of Nhulunbuy (Gove), a fly-in camp or lodge, or a mothership.

p: Nhulunbuy has hotels and motels but no camping grounds or caravan parks, and some anglers barge their boats from Darwin. Lodges and camps elsewhere are reached by light aircraft, so luggage limits are tight.

p: All of East Arnhem Land is Aboriginal land. Since 1 January 2023 the Northern Land Council has issued a free online fishing permit for intertidal waters not covered by existing access arrangements; most of the Gove Peninsula coast is covered by the Dhimurru arrangement. Visitors also need a general permit to be in Nhulunbuy, and operators usually arrange the permits their trips need.

Parts of Arnhem Land are dry areas where it is illegal to bring alcohol, and takeaway alcohol in Nhulunbuy needs a permit, so ask your operator. Crocodiles are present throughout. Check the current NT Fisheries rules for limits.

faq: How do you get to Nhulunbuy (Gove) to go fishing?

Most visitors fly: Airnorth's flight from Darwin to Gove takes about 1 hour 15 minutes (about 1 hour 50 from Cairns). Driving is about 1,044 km from Darwin, and the Central Arnhem Road needs a Northern Land Council transit permit.
Can I bring alcohol on an Arnhem Land fishing trip?

It depends where you go. Dhipirri Lodge is in a dry area where bringing alcohol is illegal, though the lodge has a licensed bar. In Nhulunbuy you need a permit to buy takeaway alcohol, and Cobourg Fishing Safaris lets guests pre-order drinks at bottle-shop prices.
How much luggage can I take on an Arnhem Land fly-in trip?

Light aircraft limit weight. Cobourg Fishing Safaris recommends no more than 15 kg in a soft bag with rod tubes under 2.4 m, and DNA Barra Fishing's island camp expects about 10 kg with rod tubes no longer than 100 cm.
Can I keep my catch on an Arnhem Land fishing trip?

Policies differ. Cobourg Fishing Safaris lets guests keep fish within NT possession limits and will vacuum-seal and freeze them, while Dhipirri Lodge keeps only what its chef needs and does not let guests take fish home.

p: The NT side of the Gulf of Carpentaria is big, remote country. Most visiting anglers come on a fly-in package to Groote Eylandt or a mothership trip on the Roper River, while self-drive anglers base themselves at Borroloola or King Ash Bay on the McArthur River.

p: Groote Eylandt is Aboriginal land managed through the Anindilyakwa Land Council; Groote Eylandt Lodge organises any permits its guests need and may change bookings at short notice for cultural or weather reasons. Elsewhere, check access and permit requirements with the Northern Land Council before you go.
Saltwater crocodiles are present throughout the Gulf rivers and King Ash Bay advises against swimming. Check the current NT Fisheries rules for bag and size limits.

faq: How do you get to Groote Eylandt for fishing?
Fly with Airnorth from Darwin. Groote Eylandt Lodge's 2–5 day fishing packages include return flights, twin-share rooms, all meals, island transfers and any permits needed.
How far is Borroloola from Darwin?
About 12 hours' drive south-east of Darwin, near the Queensland border; from Katherine it is about 7 hours via the Carpentaria Highway. Scheduled flights are also available.
Can you catch billfish in the Gulf of Carpentaria?

Yes. NT tourism says the grounds south of Groote Eylandt are known for large numbers of marlin and sailfish, mainly from November to March, and that billfish are found in good numbers close to the Sir Edward Pellew Islands.
Do I need a permit to fish Groote Eylandt?
Permits are needed to access some land on Groote, which is managed through the Anindilyakwa Land Council. If you fish with Groote Eylandt Lodge, the lodge organises the permits for you.

p: Most NT charter fishing happens in the Top End, within a day's travel of Darwin, with fly-in lodges and motherships reaching the remote coasts of Arnhem Land and the Gulf.

p: The Top End runs on wet and dry seasons rather than four, and fishing follows them.

Floodplains drain into the rivers and creeks; the peak time for trophy barramundi

p: Visiting or fishing Aboriginal land and waters often needs a permit, from the Northern Land Council, the Tiwi Land Council, the Anindilyakwa Land Council (Groote) or Dhimurru (Gove). Kakadu needs a Parks Australia pass, and most other NT parks need an NT Parks Visitor Pass. Guided trips often include these, so ask your operator.

Saltwater crocodiles live in almost all Top End waterways: be Crocwise and never swim. Bag and size limits and some area closures apply, so check the current NT Fisheries rules or the free NT Fishing Mate app before keeping fish.

faq: What is the barra run-off?

The run-off happens at the end of the wet season, roughly February or March to May, when floodwaters drain off the floodplains into the rivers and creeks. Bait is flushed out and barramundi gather at creek mouths and drains to feed, which makes it the best time of year for a fish over a metre.
Do I need a permit to fish in the Northern Territory?

You don't need a recreational fishing licence, but much of the coast is Aboriginal land, and visiting it often needs a permit from the relevant land council. Fishing with a licensed operator is usually the simplest way, as many include or arrange permits.
Are there crocodiles where NT fishing charters go?

Yes. Saltwater crocodiles are found in Darwin Harbour, the Top End rivers and billabongs, and around the islands. Guided boats are a safe way to fish, but never swim, keep back from the water's edge and follow your guide's advice.

p: Cairns charters work four very different kinds of water: the Great Barrier Reef offshore, Trinity Inlet on the city's doorstep, the Mulgrave and Russell rivers to the south, and Lake Tinaroo up on the Atherton Tablelands. Shared reef boats usually fish 30–60 m of water within about 50 km of Cairns.
Further out, the reef edge and continental shelf between Cairns and Lizard Island is where giant black marlin gather each spring.

p: Great Barrier Reef trips attract the Environmental Management Charge (reef tax): $8.50 per person from 1 April 2026 and $9 from 1 April 2027. Some operators include it, others add it, and several reef boats now add a fuel levy.

Coral trout, emperors, cods and other coral reef fin fish are closed around the October and November new moons (8–12 October and 6–10 November in 2026), and Spanish mackerel north of 22°S are closed for three weeks from each of those dates. East-coast barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January, and it is illegal to target them even for catch and release. Saltwater crocodiles live in Trinity Inlet and the rivers, so keep well back from the water's edge.

faq: How long does it take to reach the Great Barrier Reef from Cairns?
Shared reef boats allow at least 90 minutes each way and usually fish within about 50 km of Cairns. Light-tackle game boats find juvenile black marlin within about an hour's run of the city.
When is giant black marlin season in Cairns?

Peak season runs from early September to mid-December along about 150 nautical miles of reef edge between Cairns and Lizard Island. Most anglers book liveaboard trips of three to seven days, and most fish are tagged and released.
Where can I catch barramundi near Cairns?

Guides fish Trinity Inlet beside the city and the Mulgrave and Russell rivers about 40 km south, and Lake Tinaroo on the Tablelands holds metre-plus stocked barramundi. Saltwater barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January.
Is there a reef tax on Cairns fishing charters?
Yes. The Great Barrier Reef Environmental Management Charge is $8.50 per person from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, then $9. Check whether your charter price includes it.

p: Most fishing grounds around the Whitsunday Islands sit in 40–70 m of water, a 15–45 minute run from Hamilton Island, with shoals and inner reefs close to Airlie Beach. The outer Great Barrier Reef is about 40 nautical miles from Airlie Beach, so it is usually fished on full-day or extended private trips.

p: Shared trips usually supply rods, reels and bait, and most boats clean or fillet legal catch to take home. Several Hamilton Island restaurants will cook your catch. Many private trips include hotel transfers.

On reef fin fish closure days some boats run private sport or game trips only. Operators will not sail in unsafe conditions (one Airlie Beach boat never goes out under a strong wind warning), and some confirm trips 24 hours ahead. Skippers apply Queensland size and bag limits, so undersized fish go back.

faq: Can you fish the outer Great Barrier Reef from Airlie Beach?

Yes, in good weather. The outer reef is about 40 nautical miles from Airlie Beach, so it is fished on 8-hour private or 10–11 hour extended trips. Half-day and shared trips fish the island grounds and shoals.
How deep is the water around the Whitsunday Islands?
Most fishing grounds around the islands are 40–70 m deep, depending on location.
Can I go fishing in the Whitsundays during the October and November closures?

Bottom fishing for coral reef fin fish is closed 8–12 October and 6–10 November 2026, and Spanish mackerel 8–29 October and 6–27 November. Some Hamilton Island boats run private sport or game trips on those days instead.
When is sailfish season in the Whitsundays?
Sailfish are caught all year but peak from about August to December. Hamilton Island game boats target them on light tackle and tag and release them.

p: Port Douglas is about 60 km north of Cairns, under an hour's drive. Shared reef boats cap fishing numbers (MV Norseman takes 20 anglers) and gut and bag your catch, as filleting on board isn't permitted. Big boats often have a licensed bar and no BYO, while small sportfishing boats usually allow your own drinks.

Reef trips can switch to the estuaries when the wind is up. Bottom-fishing reef tours stop during the coral reef fin fish closures, and Spanish mackerel are closed for three weeks from 8 October and 6 November 2026. Crocodiles live in the local rivers and estuaries.

faq: How far is the reef from Port Douglas?
Most reef grounds are about an hour's run on the larger charter boats, and local operators say Port Douglas gives closer access to the outer reef than Cairns.
Can I keep my fish on a Port Douglas reef trip?
Yes, legal-size fish within bag limits. Shared reef boats such as MV Norseman gut and bag your catch for you to take home, but they cannot fillet on board.
What do Port Douglas fishing charters do in windy weather?
Small-boat reef trips move into the estuaries and rivers, where barramundi, mangrove jack, fingermark and grunter are on offer. Larger boats such as the 18 m Norseman handle rougher seas.
When can you catch black marlin from Port Douglas?
Juvenile black marlin are targeted on light tackle from about July to October, and giant black marlin from September to mid-December between Cairns and Lizard Island, usually on liveaboard trips.

p: Many Mackay creeks are shallow and only the larger systems can be entered at dead low tide, so guides plan trips around the tide.

Barramundi in tidal waters are closed from 1 November to 31 January, but the stocked dams stay open. Mackay is north of 22°S, so the northern Spanish mackerel closures apply: 8–29 October and 6–27 November in 2026. Estuarine crocodiles occur in Mackay's creeks and rivers.

faq: What is the Mackay Net Free Zone?

A net-free stretch of coast from Cape Hillsborough to the northern end of St Helens Bay, covering fifteen creek systems plus inlets, beaches and mangrove flats. It holds barramundi, grunter, mangrove jack and salmon, with all-tide ramps at Victor Creek, Seaforth and Murray Creek.
Can you catch barramundi in Mackay during the closed season?
Yes, in the stocked dams. Teemburra, Kinchant and Eungella dams stay open while saltwater barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January; the afternoon, dusk and night bites are best.
Where do Mackay reef charters fish?

Around island groups in 30–40 m of water (Sir James Smith, Cumberland and Beverley), out past Scawfell Island where red fish appear at about 50 m, and at Great Barrier Reef anchorages such as Square, Stevens and Chauvel reefs.
Is there fly fishing in Mackay?
Yes. A local guide runs fly and lure trips on the Seaforth flats for golden trevally, queenfish, permit and blackspot tuskfish, and on Kinchant and Teemburra dams for barramundi.

p: Long reef trips usually supply bait, tackle, ice and water but not main meals, so bring your own food. Individual seats are sold on mixed-group trips that are opened when the weather suits, often at short notice through social media.

Magnetic Island charters are private only, with up to five guests inshore and four offshore, and guests can bring their own food and drinks. Townsville waters are within crocodile habitat, so take care around estuaries.

faq: How long does it take to reach the reef from Townsville?
About 1.5–2 hours from Breakwater Marina to the first reef drop on a fast charter boat, depending on the weather. That is why most Townsville reef trips run 12–13 hours or longer.
Can I join a Townsville reef trip on my own?
Yes. Mixed-group charters sell individual spots on 12–13 hour reef trips with up to 12 people. They are opened when the weather suits and need to fill before they go.
Can you fish around Magnetic Island?

Yes. Of the island's 23 bays and beaches, 14 are fishable, with wrecks, shoals, fringing reef and mangroves. Charters from Horseshoe Bay troll for spotted mackerel and tuna and bottom fish for coral trout and tuskfish.

p: The river is home to plenty of saltwater crocodiles and rich birdlife, so many fishing trips double as nature tours. Keep away from the water's edge, keep hands inside the boat and bin fish scraps.

Barramundi are closed on Queensland's east coast from 1 November to 31 January, and deliberately targeting them, even for catch and release, is prohibited. River trips use small boats for two to three anglers or a shaded catamaran for families, and most supply bait and tackle; bring your own food and drinks on the share trips.

faq: Are there crocodiles in the Daintree River?
Yes. The river has plenty of saltwater crocodiles and spotting them is part of many fishing trips. Follow your guide's instructions, stay back from the water's edge and keep limbs inside the boat.
Can you fish the Daintree for barramundi in November?

No. The east-coast barramundi closed season runs from 1 November to 31 January, and deliberately targeting barra, even catch and release, is prohibited then. Guides switch to mangrove jack and other species.
Can Daintree fishing trips go out to the reef?
On calm days, yes. Guides can add Snapper Island, nearby wrecks and inshore reefs at the river mouth for coral trout and Spanish mackerel, usually on three-quarter or full-day trips.

p: Most visitors book five-to-seven-day all-inclusive packages with transfers, meals and accommodation, and fishing is largely catch and release. Mobile coverage reaches only about 10 km from town, so expect to be out of range on the water.
Weipa waters hold crocodiles, box jellyfish, stonefish, sharks and stingrays, so wade only where your guide says it's safe. Gulf barramundi have a closed season starting on 7 October.

faq: How do you get to Weipa for a fishing trip?

Fly from Cairns: QantasLink flies to Weipa twice daily on most days, a flight of about an hour. Luggage is limited to one 23 kg item, so tape rod tubes to your bag. Guides usually include airport transfers.
Can you fly fish in Weipa?

Yes. Weipa is a well-known saltwater fly destination, with permit, blue bastards, golden trevally and queenfish on the flats, barramundi and threadfin in the estuaries, and pelagics on offshore bait balls. One local operation now runs fly-only trips.
Is fishing in Weipa catch and release?
Mostly. Local guides run largely catch-and-release operations, but you can usually eat fish during your stay, and some allow a small package to take home.
Is there phone reception when fishing out of Weipa?
Coverage reaches only about 10 km from the town centre, so expect to be out of range on the water. Guide boats carry VHF radios, and long-range trips carry a satellite phone.

p: Karumba is remote, so most visiting anglers either fly into Normanton and transfer by road or drive across from the east coast. Local charters supply gear and bait, and many allow BYO alcohol in cans.

Barramundi can't be targeted during the Gulf closed season, which starts on 7 October. One local charter keeps catch on ice but, citing Queensland rules, does not fillet on board. The Gulf is crocodile country, so stay back from the water's edge.

faq: When can you fish for barramundi in Karumba?

Dedicated barramundi charters run from February to April and again from September until 7 October, when the Gulf closed season starts. Outside those windows charters target threadfin, jewfish, mackerel and other species.
How far offshore do Karumba fishing charters go?
Offshore trips run about 40–50 km into the Gulf of Carpentaria for Spanish mackerel, cobia, fingermark, trevally and queenfish, weather permitting.
How do I get to Karumba for a fishing trip?
Fly into Normanton and transfer to Karumba by road; some multi-day packages include the transfer. Many anglers also drive across from the east coast.

p: Launch at Dungeness from half tide up: near low tide the end of the ramp can be almost exposed, and on big tides the channel bar can't be crossed for about two hours either side of low. Lucinda is about 1.5 hours' drive north of Townsville and 2.5 hours south of Cairns.

The channel is within the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and World Heritage Area, so check zoning maps; green zones are no-take. Estuarine crocodiles live in the channel and creeks: keep back from the bank, don't wade in for snagged lures and bin your fish frames.

faq: Can I fish for barramundi year-round in the Hinchinbrook Channel?
No. Barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January. Mangrove jack, fingermark, threadfin salmon and other species stay open, so guides keep fishing through the closure.
When is the best tide to launch at the Dungeness ramp in Lucinda?
Half tide to high tide. Near low tide the end of the ramp can be almost exposed, and on big tides the channel bar can be impassable for about two hours either side of low.
Where is Missionary Bay?
At the northern end of Hinchinbrook Island. It is a large protected waterway with nine creeks, deep holes and rock bars, and charters reach it by launching from Cardwell.
How far is the Hinchinbrook Channel from Townsville?
About 1.5 hours' drive north of Townsville to Lucinda, and about 2.5 hours south of Cairns. Some guides include Townsville Airport transfers with multi-day packages.

p: Nearly every Gold Coast offshore charter heads out through the Gold Coast Seaway. Half-day boats fish reefs about 10-20 km offshore in 33-50 m of water, around 15-30 minutes from the Seaway, while full days push 10-35 km out into 50-95 m. Calm-water charters stay inside on the Broadwater and the rivers.

p: Reef charters run all year. Snapper are caught year-round, with bigger fish in the cooler months, and the warm East Australian Current brings pelagics close to the coast in summer. Humpback whales pass between June and October and are often seen from fishing boats.

p: Most shared offshore trips last five hours, with an early-morning and a late-morning or afternoon departure; seven- and nine-hour days head wider. Boats leave on time and won't wait for latecomers. Rain alone rarely cancels a trip, but strong wind and swell do, and the call is usually made the afternoon or evening before.

Catch handling varies by boat: some crews clean and bag your fish, but Fish The Deep doesn't clean fish and legally can't fillet, so bring an esky and leave it in the car. Queensland limits apply on every boat; for example, snapper must be at least 35 cm, with four per person and only one over 70 cm.

faq: How far offshore do Gold Coast fishing charters go?

Half-day trips typically fish reefs about 10-20 km out in 33-50 m of water, 15-30 minutes from the Seaway. Full days run 10-35 km offshore into 50-95 m, although strong December-January currents can force boats back onto the closer grounds.
Are there calm-water fishing trips on the Gold Coast?

Yes. Small-boat charters fish the Broadwater, Nerang River and Jumpinpin for flathead, whiting, bream and mangrove jack, a good option for kids or rough days. BKs runs private calm-water trips for up to three people from Runaway Bay or Paradise Point.
Can you see whales on a Gold Coast fishing charter?

Yes, in season. Humpback whales migrate past the Gold Coast from June to October, and operators such as BKs and True Blue mention whales during fishing trips. BKs and Hooker 1 also run dedicated whale-watching tours.
What is the minimum age on Gold Coast fishing charters?
It depends on the boat. BKs takes children from six, while True Blue and Fish The Deep set a minimum age of seven on shared trips; True Blue takes younger children on private bookings.
gold-coast.season: Reef fishing runs all year, with the better snapper in the cooler months (snapper and pearl perch are closed to take from 15 July to 15 August). From about November to February the East Australian Current brings marlin, sailfish, wahoo, mahi mahi and tuna within reach, though strong December-January currents can keep full-day boats on the closer reefs.

Lure and calm-water guides fish inside the bay, the Brisbane River and the Pumicestone Passage.

p: Offshore days start early, around 4:30-5:30am depending on the season, and weather confirmations are given the afternoon or evening before. Some boats keep the catch whole: Moreton Island Fishing Charters can't process seafood on board and Frenzy Charters keeps fish whole in an ice slurry, so leave an esky in the car.

Moreton Bay is a marine park: Scarborough Reef is a yellow (conservation park) zone and Scotts Point is a green zone. Queensland limits apply, including a 35 cm minimum and four-per-person possession limit for snapper (only one over 70 cm).

faq: How long does it take to reach the offshore grounds from Brisbane?

From Manly, boats cross Moreton Bay and exit through the South Passage bar. Frenzy Charters puts the run at about 1 hour 15 minutes, or around 2.5 hours for continental-shelf trips, which is why most Brisbane offshore charters are full days only.
Can a Brisbane charter pick me up from North Stradbroke Island?

Yes. Frenzy Charters and Moreton Island Fishing Charters both offer pick-ups from Amity Point by arrangement. Moreton Island Fishing Charters can also collect from the Bay Islands, and from Moreton Island on private charters.
Are there calm-water fishing trips near Brisbane for kids?

Yes. Fish Moreton runs two- and four-hour smooth-water trips in the Pumicestone Passage behind Bribie Island for flathead, bream, whiting and tailor, and Brisbane Fishing Tour guides private lure-fishing trips for one to four people on Moreton Bay and the Brisbane River.
Why do Brisbane charters switch to trolling in summer?

A strong East Australian Current combined with northerly winds can make it hard to fish the bottom, so operators such as Frenzy Charters switch to trolling for mahi mahi, wahoo, mackerel, marlin and tuna, including around the FADs.

Before fishing on your own, check size and bag limits, seasonal closures and green zones; Noosa Bluewater Charters points anglers to Great Sandy Marine Park zoning for the waters off Noosa.

faq: How far are the reefs from Noosa?

Sunshine Reef and North Reef, the half-day grounds, are about 30-45 minutes from Noosa (Deep Sea Fishing Co. quotes 20-40 minutes). Seven- and nine-hour trips run about 1.5-2 hours each way to Chardons Reef, Double Island, the Banks and the Hards.
Which Sunshine Coast charters reach the Barwon Banks?

Salty's nine-hour trip from Caloundra heads 40 km+ to the Barwon Banks, about 1-1.5 hours each way, and its 12-hour trip can reach the Hards. From Noosa, Noosa Bluewater's nine-hour trip runs out to Double Island, the Banks and the Hards.
Are there calm-water fishing trips on the Sunshine Coast?
Yes. Salty's Fishing Charters runs four-hour family trips in the northern Pumicestone Passage from Pelican Waters Marina for bream, flathead and whiting, with child and pensioner prices.
Is dawn the best time for snapper off Noosa?

Usually. Noosa Bluewater Charters says low light combined with a tide change often triggers a feeding spell that doesn't last all day, so dawn tends to beat mid-morning, and late autumn through winter is the best season.
sunshine-coast.season: Reef fishing runs all year, but May to October is the prime window, with snapper best from late autumn through winter (snapper and pearl perch are closed to take from 15 July to 15 August). Rainbow Beach Fishing Charters' skipper weighs wind, swell and bar conditions, and weather-cancelled trips are moved to a new date.

Neither boat has EFTPOS on board, so pay ahead. Bring your own lunch on the Baitrunner (cans-only BYO alcohol). Because trips are weather-dependent, book flexible accommodation; the Big4 park at Carlo Point is a short walk from the Keely Rose pontoon.

faq: Do Rainbow Beach fishing charters run half days?
Not usually. Both local operators, Keely Rose and Rainbow Beach Fishing Charters, run full days only, leaving between about 5 and 5:30am and returning mid-afternoon.
Why do I need to call the day before a Rainbow Beach charter?

Departure times shift with daylight and sea conditions. Keely Rose asks every passenger to phone the day before to confirm the time and that conditions are suitable, and to check the trip is definitely going ahead before travelling to Rainbow Beach.
Where should I stay for an early charter at Rainbow Beach?

Keely Rose points to the Big4 Breeze Holiday Park at Carlo Point, a short walk from its boat, along with other parks and resorts in town. As trips depend on the weather, Rainbow Beach Fishing Charters recommends flexible or refundable accommodation.
Can I pay by card on a Rainbow Beach charter boat?

No. Keely Rose needs payment by card or bank deposit at least 24 hours before the trip, and Rainbow Beach Fishing Charters asks for bank-transfer balances 48 hours before departure, as neither boat has EFTPOS.

p: Hervey Bay charters work a huge, shallow bay sheltered by K'gari (Fraser Island). Half days stay inshore around the bay islands, sand flats, Great Sandy Strait and inner reefs; full days run up the western side of K'gari, and specialist trips make the long run to Breaksea Spit at the island's northern tip.
